meta.title: Three Notes for Saturday
meta.textType: functional: three notes with times and places

paragraphs: On Friday, August seventh, at six o'clock, Lily finds three notes in the kitchen. They are three short messages about Saturday. Two notes are on the table, next to her school bag. One note is on the fridge. The first note is from Teacher Kim. It says, "Dear parents, the Explorers go to the science museum tomorrow, Saturday, August eighth." "Please bring your child to the school gate at eight o'clock." "The bus leaves at a quarter past eight." "Please bring a snack for lunchtime at the museum." "We come back at half past twelve."

The second note is on the fridge, under a small magnet. It is from Mom. It says, "Lily, your snack and an umbrella are in your bag." "Have you packed your notebook yet?" Lily opens her bag and looks inside. She sees the snack and the umbrella. But she has not packed her notebook yet. She gets it from her room.

The third note is from Mia. Mia's math book is on the table, and Mia's note is on top of it. It says, "I'll wait at your gate at twenty to eight." "Please bring back my math book." Lily has the book, and she wants to bring it back. She takes a pencil and a piece of paper. Then she writes a list in time order. "Twenty to eight, my gate." "Eight o'clock, school gate." "A quarter past eight, bus." "Half past twelve, back."

Mom comes into the kitchen. "Have you read all three notes?" she asks. "Yes, and I have already made a list," says Lily. "What time does the bus leave?" asks Mom. "It leaves at a quarter past eight," says Lily. "What time do you leave home?" asks Mom. "I leave at twenty to eight with Mia," says Lily. "Remember Mia's math book," says Mom. "Do not forget it!" "I have already put it in my bag," says Lily.
After supper, Lily reads her list again. Her bag has the snack, the umbrella, the notebook, and the math book. Tomorrow is a big day for the Explorers. She goes to bed early.
text.summary: On Friday evening, Lily finds three notes with times and places for a trip. She reads them, makes a list in time order, and packs her bag.
